summary: Milestone 2026.09.666 executed 7 experiments, all compute-bound, totaling 6.0 wall-time minutes. The longest experiment was 'Protect goal checks in reusable ARC planner deduplication' at 2.68 minutes, followed by 'Reconcile fourteen outcomes and decide evidence and planner scope' at 0.9 minutes and 'Expose the measured native service as an opt-in typed consumer' at 0.82 minutes. Intra-experiment phase durations were not recorded, so internal execution stages could not be individually assessed.
bottlenecks_identified: The top-ranking experiment 'Protect goal checks in reusable ARC planner deduplication' took 2.68 minutes (approximately 44.7% of the 6.0 total wall-time minutes), but absence of sub-stage profiling prevents determining whether planner search, model execution, or goal-guard verification dominated.

The three slowest compute-bound tasks ('Protect goal checks in reusable ARC planner deduplication' at 2.68 minutes, 'Reconcile fourteen outcomes and decide evidence and planner scope' at 0.9 minutes, and 'Expose the measured native service as an opt-in typed consumer' at 0.82 minutes) consumed 4.40 out of 6.0 total wall-time minutes (73.3%) without intra-task stage timing.
The 5 slowest experiments together accounted for 5.47 of the 6.0 total wall-time minutes (91.2%), with experiment runtimes reconstructed from disk mtime rather than active wall-clock interval traces.

The GPU monitor report provides an isolated post-execution state (both GPU 0 and GPU 1 at 4MB allocated, 0% utilization, 49C and 43C), giving no visibility into live accelerator duty cycles during task execution while gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false.
No experiment execution records indicate running two or more models concurrently, rendering DualGPURunner dispatch inapplicable for this milestone's tasks.
improvements_suggested: Introduce monotonic sub-phase timers inside compute-bound pipelines—particularly planner deduplication and native consumer wrappers—to quantify time spent in model evaluation versus validation checks.
Capture continuous in-run GPU telemetry during compute-bound executions to evaluate accelerator utilization and VRAM dynamics across active task windows.
Include model inventory and concurrency metadata in experiment execution manifests to verify DualGPURunner eligibility when multiple models are executed.
Persist structured milestone run logs with exact start and end timestamps to avoid falling back to disk-mtime timing reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument sub-phase duration counters in the ARC planner deduplication and native consumer paths to break down compute overhead.
Implement continuous GPU utilization logging during compute-bound task runs to record active-window accelerator metrics.
Log model concurrency and runner dispatch decisions in experiment receipts to audit DualGPURunner usage on multi-model workloads.
meta_reflection: Across 6.0 wall-time minutes, milestone 2026.09.666 completed 7 compute-bound experiments led by planner deduplication (2.68 minutes) and capstone outcome reconciliation (0.9 minutes). Although the point-in-time GPU snapshot showed both GPUs idle with 4MB allocated, gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false and in-run accelerator utilization was unmeasured, with no multi-model tasks present to engage DualGPURunner. Implementing fine-grained intra-task phase instrumentation and continuous accelerator monitoring provides the clearest operational path to diagnosing bottlenecks in subsequent milestones.
